It also adds result_value == split_amount, the decrement identity, and pool_id preservation on both the original and the result, so the function's behavioral contract is now fully characterized rather than only abort-free. The capture method is correct: fungible_staked_sui_value returns u64 by value, so the let-binding snapshots the pre-call value; clone! (suggested in the issue) is unnecessary for a scalar and the value-capture is semantically equivalent. No assertion was weakened -- the original asserts(split_amount <= original_value) guard is preserved verbatim, so abort coverage is intact and no regression was introduced.
